requirement_text: Applicants must apply using one of three platforms: the Common Application, the Coalition Application on SCOIR, or the QuestBridge Application.
researcher_notes: Platform names (Common Application / Coalition Application on SCOIR / QuestBridge Application) are each named verbatim on the source page; the connecting sentence is this researcher's summary of a list, hence extracted_summary. Cross-confirmed on admissions.yale.edu/apply. 'Yale does not advantage students who apply through any program' per admissions.yale.edu/apply — platform choice itself carries no admissions weight.

requirement_text: All first-year and transfer applicants must include scores from the ACT or SAT.
limitations: Yale publishes no minimum SAT/ACT score; this is a submission requirement evaluated holistically, not a scalar threshold, so test_scale is left null even though SAT/ACT are scaled tests — there is no cutoff to qualify with a scale.
researcher_notes: CURRENT POLICY as of retrieval (2026-08-21), confirmed on two independent live official pages (admissions.yale.edu/requirements and admissions.yale.edu/standardized-testing) and corroborated by the official announcement at news.yale.edu/2026/05/27/undergraduate-admissions-updates-testing-policy, which states: 'Beginning with the next admissions cycle, applicants will be required to submit scores from the ACT or SAT.' That announcement is dated 2026-05-27 (before this cycle's Nov 1 2026 SCEA deadline), so 'the next admissions cycle' unambiguously denotes the 2026-27 cycle / Fall 2027 entry (cycle_year 2027), which is the cycle this research batch targets. Third-party sources (Yale Daily News, admissions-consulting blogs) label this the 'Class of 2031' policy; that exact phrase was not found verbatim on the official announcement page itself in this session's fetch, so it is reported here as third-party framing, not as a literal Yale quote. Supersedes the 2024-2026 test-flexible policy (see REQ-2026-08-21-YAL0004).

requirement_text: AP or IB scores (optional but encouraged if completed).
researcher_notes: IMPORTANT POLICY-HISTORY FINDING, directly responsive to the brief's flagged trap. AP/IB exam scores do NOT currently fulfill Yale's testing requirement on their own — SAT or ACT is mandatory (REQ-YAL0002), and AP/IB is supplementary only. This is a REVERSAL of the 2024-2026 'test-flexible' policy, under which AP/IB scores COULD substitute for SAT/ACT (see REQ-2026-08-21-YAL0004, VERIFIED_HISTORICAL). The official reversal announcement (news.yale.edu/2026/05/27/undergraduate-admissions-updates-testing-policy) states explicitly: 'The previous test-flexible policy permitted applicants to fulfil the testing requirement with scores from four options: ACT, Advanced Placement (AP), International Baccalaureate (IB), or SAT,' and that the new policy 'no longer accepts AP or IB scores as alternatives.' Do not conflate this current record with the historical one — a student reading only the 2024 announcement (still live, see YAL0004) would be misinformed about the current cycle's actual requirement.

requirement_text: It will expand the list of tests that fulfill the requirement to include AP and IB exams in addition to the SAT and ACT.
limitations: Applied to the 2024-25 and 2025-26 admissions cycles (entry Fall 2025 and Fall 2026 — spans two entry years, so cycle_year is left null rather than picking one). Superseded 2026-05-27 for the 2026-27 cycle (entry Fall 2027, cycle_year 2027) onward. NOT applicable to the current cycle this research batch targets.
researcher_notes: DILIGENCE NOTE on the brief's 'two live official pages that both look current' trap: this page (news.yale.edu/2024/02/22/...) IS still live and fetchable as of 2026-08-21, but it is a dated news article (dated 22 Feb 2024 in its own URL and byline), not an evergreen/undated requirements page, so a reader encountering it understands it is reporting a Feb-2024 change rather than announcing today's policy — this researcher does NOT classify it as CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE against REQ-YAL0002/0003. The page that would most plausibly have caused a genuine same-looking-current conflict — an undated explainer titled 'test-flexible-counselors' at admissions.yale.edu/test-flexible-counselors, which Google still had indexed at time of search — returned HTTP 404 on direct fetch during this session (2026-08-21), i.e. it has been taken down. A dev-subdomain mirror (dev.admissions.yale.edu/faq/standardized-testing) also appeared in search results but returned HTTP 503 on every fetch attempt this session and could not be read; this is recorded as an unresolved ACCESS LIMITATION, not a confirmed conflict — per evidence rule 2 ('search discovers, fetch verifies'), its content is not asserted either way. No live evergreen page asserting test-optional or the old test-flexible-as-current was found and successfully fetched. Full policy chronology found this session: pre-2020 required → 2020-2024 test-optional (pandemic, ~4 cycles) → 2024-2026 test-flexible (SAT/ACT/AP/IB all fulfilled the requirement, this record) → 2026-05-27 onward: SAT/ACT required again, AP/IB supplementary only (REQ-YAL0002/0003).

requirement_text: Two teachers who have taught you recently in core academic subjects (English, mathematics, science, social studies, or a foreign language); computer science, engineering, art history, philosophy, psychology, research, and journalism are also considered core academic subjects. Also required: a letter from your school's college counselor, or a school administrator if your school does not have a counselor.
researcher_notes: Two teacher recommendations plus one counselor (or administrator) recommendation — three letters total.

requirement_text: School Report with an official transcript that includes all completed secondary school courses. High school seniors must also submit a Mid-Year Report with official grades from the first marking period of senior year.

Challenge yourself with a balanced academic program that includes demanding courses in a wide range of subjects. [Applicants are evaluated] within their own context, so that no student is disadvantaged for not taking advantage of a resource that was not available to them. We only expect you to take advantage of such courses if your high school provides them.
limitations: No minimum GPA, class rank, or specific-subject/year-count coursework requirement is published — this is a deliberate 'no scalar exists' finding, not a gap in this research. Text fidelity is extracted_summary because the fetch tool paraphrased around several short verbatim fragments rather than returning one continuous quoted passage; the bracketed fragments above are the verbatim pieces.
researcher_notes: Recorded per evidence rule 6 ('unknown/absent is a valid result'): Yale's transcript/course-rigor evaluation is explicitly holistic and contextual to each applicant's school, with no published numeric threshold to store as structured_rule.

requirement_text: If you are a non-native English-speaker graduating from secondary school where English is not the language of instruction, also submit results from an English proficiency test. Accepted tests: TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge English Qualifications, Duolingo English Test (DET), and InitialView.
limitations: Exemption: applicants with two or more years of enrollment in an English-medium secondary school are not required to submit an English proficiency test, per admissions.yale.edu/standardized-testing.

requirement_text: Yale's most competitive applicants typically earn a score of 5 or higher (for tests taken after January 21, 2026).
limitations: Not a published minimum — described as the typical score of Yale's most competitive applicants, not a pass/fail requirement. Unambiguous because Yale's own page explicitly scopes this figure to tests taken after the 21 Jan 2026 ETS rescale date, rather than mixing old- and new-scale figures the way another university's page did (see scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md finding #1 for the contrast case).

requirement_text: Yale's most competitive applicants typically earn ... at least 100 (for tests taken before January 21, 2026).
limitations: Not a published minimum. Applies only to score reports from tests administered before 21 Jan 2026 on the legacy 0-120 (sum of four sections) scale; still a live, actionable figure today for any applicant submitting a pre-cutover score report, so this is treated as current guidance rather than historical.
researcher_notes: Same source page as REQ-YAL0009 states both figures side by side, cleanly separated by test-date rather than conflated — unlike the Glasgow/Boğaziçi defect pattern documented in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md, Yale's own page does not require any interpretation to know which figure applies to a given score report.

requirement_text: Yale's most competitive applicants have IELTS scores of 7 or higher.
limitations: Not a published minimum — typical score of competitive applicants. IELTS scale is unaffected by the 2026 TOEFL rescale.

requirement_text: Yale's most competitive applicants have Cambridge English scores of 185 or higher on the C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency, or B2 First exams.
limitations: Not a published minimum — typical score of competitive applicants. Cambridge English Scale is unaffected by the 2026 TOEFL rescale.

requirement_text: Yale's most competitive applicants have DET (Duolingo English Test) scores of at least 120.
limitations: Not a published minimum — typical score of competitive applicants. Duolingo English Test is scored on its own 10-160 scale, but the test_scale enum provided for this research batch has no Duolingo/DET value (only TOEFL/IELTS/Cambridge/SAT variants) — left null rather than forcing an incorrect enum value. Flagging this as an enum gap for the engineering lane.

requirement_text: International applicants fulfill the same standardized testing requirements as domestic applicants. Scores from other exams, including international leaving exams or English proficiency exams, will not fulfill Yale's testing requirement. All application materials must be in English; documents in another language, including transcripts and letters of recommendation, must be accompanied by a certified translation.
researcher_notes: Confirms international applicants get no substitute path via a home-country leaving exam (e.g. cannot use a national exam in place of SAT/ACT) — the SAT/ACT requirement in REQ-YAL0002 binds international applicants identically to domestic ones.

requirement_text: A family's ability to pay is not a factor in the admissions process—for any student, anywhere in the world. Yale is one of only a handful of American universities that considers all applicants for admission without regard to their ability to pay and meets 100% of every family's demonstrated financial need.
limitations: Categorized as requirement_category_db 'supplemental_requirement' rather than 'international_requirement' — this is an admissions POLICY that benefits international applicants (need-blind evaluation + full demonstrated need met), not a requirement imposed ON international applicants, so the more specific enum value was judged a worse fit despite the international relevance.
researcher_notes: International applicants 'receive the same need-based financial aid as domestic applicants,' including housing/meals/travel allowances adjusted for cost-of-living differences between countries, per the same source page. This need-blind-for-international-students policy is notable because it is not universal among elite US universities.

requirement_text: Yale's Single-Choice Early Action Program (also called Restrictive Early Action) is non-binding. If you opt to apply through Single-Choice Early Action at Yale, you may not also apply through Early Action or Early Decision to other colleges or universities, unless: (1) The early admissions program is a non-binding rolling admission program. (2) The early admissions program is a non-binding early program at a public institution. (3) The early admissions program is an Early Decision or Early Action program that notifies applicants after January 1. (4) The early admissions program is at an institution outside the United States.
researcher_notes: This is a binding contractual commitment, not a checkable eligibility fact — should not be auto-converted into a structured_rule threshold by a future interpretation pass; needs human review to represent correctly. Yale's SCEA itself is non-binding on the STUDENT's obligation to enroll (admitted students may wait until May 1 to reply, same as Regular Decision admits) — the binding element captured in this record is the EXCLUSIVITY restriction on applying to other schools' early rounds while an SCEA application to Yale is pending, not a commitment to attend Yale. Officially termed 'Restrictive Early Action' by Yale itself. Confirmed via two independent fetches of the same live page, word-for-word identical both times. The source page does not state a specific consequence/penalty for violating the restriction.

requirement_text: For Yale and most QuestBridge partners, the match is binding. [Matched students] will withdraw all other applications and plan to matriculate at Yale. Students who do not match at any partner college will be automatically moved into Yale's regular decision application pool.
limitations: applies_to set to 'domestic' by inference, not an explicit citizenship/residency exclusion statement found on this page: QuestBridge's National College Match is generally documented (including by QuestBridge itself, a third party not independently fetched this session) as serving US-based low-income students. Corroborating evidence from an official Yale source: finaid.yale.edu/apply/prospective lists 'QuestBridge' and 'Early Action (US Citizens/Permanent Residents)' sharing the same 1 Nov financial-aid-document date, while 'Early Action (International Citizens)' gets a separate, later date — implying Yale's own financial aid office groups QuestBridge applicants with domestic EA applicants. Not confirmed against QuestBridge's own eligibility rules directly in this session.
researcher_notes: This is a binding contractual commitment, not a checkable eligibility fact — should not be auto-converted into a structured_rule threshold by a future interpretation pass; needs human review to represent correctly. Unlike SCEA, QuestBridge National College Match IS a genuine commitment-to-enroll: a matched student agrees to withdraw all other pending applications and matriculate at Yale, materially different from SCEA's non-binding reply-by-May-1 structure (REQ-YAL0016). Matching students may request to postpone matriculation by one year; unmatched applicants are released from any commitment and automatically rolled into the Regular Decision pool.

requirement_text: Tell us about a topic or idea that excites you and is related to one or more academic areas you selected above. Why are you drawn to it? (200 words or fewer)
limitations: Essay prompts are known to change between application cycles at Yale; this source page does not itself state which cycle these prompts govern. Retrieved live on 2026-08-21, ahead of the 1 Nov 2026 SCEA deadline, and presumed to be the active prompts for the current cycle, but not explicitly cycle-labeled by Yale — hence VERIFIED_UNDATED rather than VERIFIED_CURRENT.
researcher_notes: Required of all first-year applicants regardless of platform; preceded by a selection of up to three academic areas of interest from a fixed list.

requirement_text: Short Takes (each response limited to 200 characters, approximately 35 words): 1. If you could teach any college course, write a book, or create an original piece of art of any kind, what would it be? 2. What is one aspect of yourself that you hope to grow or develop during college? 3. What is something about you that is not included anywhere else in your application?
limitations: Same cycle-labeling caveat as REQ-YAL0018. Reported (via the same fetch) as required on the Common Application and Coalition Application; not independently confirmed whether the QuestBridge Application platform carries the identical three prompts.

requirement_text: Respond to one of the following prompts in 400 words or fewer: 1. Reflect on a time you discussed an issue important to you with someone holding an opposing view. Why did you find the experience meaningful? 2. Reflect on your membership in a community to which you feel connected. Why is this community meaningful to you? 3. Reflect on an element of your personal experience that you feel will enrich your college. How has it shaped you?
limitations: Same cycle-labeling caveat as REQ-YAL0018. Reported as required on the Common Application and Coalition Application; not independently confirmed for the QuestBridge Application platform.

requirement_text: All Yale interviews are evaluative. Interviews are by invitation only and not required. The Yale Alumni Schools Committee (ASC) conducts interviews wherever there is a local association of alumni volunteers; a small group of Yale seniors also serve as Senior Interviewers. Because of limited interviewing capacity, the Office of Undergraduate Admissions prioritizes interviews for students for whom the Admissions Committee would value additional information. Not receiving an interview invitation is not an indication that your application is not competitive, and many successful applicants are not interviewed. Applicants may not request an interview; interviews are by invitation only.

Yale does not issue its own fee waivers, but it is easy to apply for free if you meet any of the eligibility criteria for your chosen application platform. U.S. military veterans and active-duty service members receive automatic application fee waivers.
limitations: Exact application fee dollar amount could not be directly fetch-verified from an official Yale page in this research session (admissions.yale.edu/cost-and-financial-aid returned HTTP 404; a $80 figure appeared only in third-party/search-synthesis text attributed to admissions.yale.edu, never confirmed by an actual successful fetch of a Yale page stating it, so per evidence rule 2 it is excluded from this record rather than recorded at low confidence).
